purpose: Close force-generation and scheduling questions before simulating HAILSTONE and CATCHPOLE from the re-run FLINTLOCK state.

closed_conclusions.US_ground_force_delta: No theater-level manpower or armor delta large enough to reopen FLINTLOCK or cancel/rewrite CATCHPOLE. Replacement/cadre differences remain unit-quality effects, not division-count effects.
closed_conclusions.US_amphibious_vehicle_delta: CATCHPOLE has a dedicated reserve assault wallet. FLINTLOCK LVT losses do not automatically debit the 106 amtracs + 17 amphibian tanks assigned to the reserve force.
closed_conclusions.5Feb_LST_hit: The unnamed FLINTLOCK southern-echelons LST mission-kill is a theater tug/repair/escort burden, not an automatic -1 from the dedicated CATCHPOLE nine-LST wallet.
closed_conclusions.HAILSTONE_CATCHPOLE_parallelism: The two operations can proceed in parallel because their principal air/fire-support wallets are separable, but DD/ASW, tanker, replacement-aircraft and command-attention competition remains real.
closed_conclusions.Japan_Eniwetok_reinforcement: No additional large reinforcement convoy is centered after Kwajalein falls. Existing garrison adapts in place; mobile personnel and high-value shipping are preserved westward instead of being fed into a nearly isolated atoll.
closed_conclusions.Japan_carrier_counterattack: No first-line carrier reversal toward Truk/Eniwetok is centered. Four hulls survive, but Feb-2 aircrew/cadre debt and the absence of a positive-EV fresh TF58 geometry make preservation westward dominant.

schedule.HAILSTONE_second_day: 1944-02-21 expected if Truk fixed air-defense/base system remains operational enough to require continued neutralization; not a scripted result
schedule.Eniwetok_and_Parry_follow_on: OPEN after Engebi/captured-intelligence state; do not pre-script simultaneous or historical sequencing

historical_process_anchors: Historical HAILSTONE attacked Truk 17-18 Feb after TF58 replenishment at Majuro and sortie on 12-13 Feb.
Historical HAILSTONE main strike used nine fast-carrier decks while TG58.4 supported Eniwetok.
Historical CATCHPOLE used a separate reserve assault formation and proceeded in parallel with HAILSTONE.
Historical Eniwetok planning was revised after captured documents showed more defenders than expected; follow-on island sequencing therefore remains a live decision variable.
branch_guards: Enterprise CV-6 and Saratoga CV-3 are permanent Branch Midway losses; never reinsert them.
Cabot CVL-28 remains campaign-out from the 2-Feb carrier battle.
Do not turn dedicated CATCHPOLE reserve gear into free reinforcement for other operations.
Do not back-port Palau/Marianas deep-defense maturity into February Eniwetok.
Do not force HAILSTONE historical surprise or historical Truk shipping massacre; Branch warning and evacuation are active.
